title: Why Roads Lean: tan θ = v²/rg Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A race track tilts at its curves, and so do flyover ramps and cycling tracks. A leaning road looks unsafe, so why build one? Aarav rides up the flyover near college and sees the curve tilt, its outer edge higher. Why tilt it, and how much tilt is just right? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we learn the banking of roads.

A live car on a banked curve, seen from behind, shows the normal force tilting with the road. Its sideways part, N sin θ, points to the centre and turns the car. Tilt the road from 0 to 35 degrees and the ideal speed climbs a curve on the graph. A slow-mo replay at 20 degrees shows friction at zero at the ideal speed, down the slope when the car goes faster and up the slope when it goes slower. We derive tan θ = v²/rg and the top speed with friction, v = √(rg(μ + tan θ)/(1 - μ tan θ)), step by step, compare a flat road with a banked one, answer two pause-and-think questions and follow the flyover link by link. Then a worked example on the flyover, the exam trap N = mg cos θ, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Curves that lean, and Aarav's flyover
0:25 What is banking?
0:48 Live simulation: tilt the road, the normal force turns the car
1:35 tan θ = v²/rg and the top speed, step by step
2:24 Flat road vs banked road + pause and think
3:17 Why tilt the flyover, link by link
3:38 Worked example: the flyover curve
4:18 Exam trap: is N = mg cos θ?
4:38 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:24 Recap and three questions to answer
